analysis.title: Mobileye Global Inc. (MBLY): Progress with eyes-on ADAS awards; execution on robotaxi business and humanoids, plus outlook for its VW business, will likely be key from here; 3Q26 wrap
key_insights: Mobileye 3Q26 revenue/EBIT/non-GAAP EPS of $492 mn/$89 mn/$0.12 beat FactSet consensus ($477 mn/$78 mn/$0.10) and GS ($477 mn/$81 mn/$0.10).
FY26 guidance midpoints raised for revenue and adjusted operating income, but the updated guidance is roughly in line with the Street.
Implied 4Q26 guidance at the midpoint (revenue $450 mn, non-GAAP EBIT $61 mn, margin 13.6%) is below the Street ($463 mn, $73 mn, 15.8%) and about in line with GS prior ($449 mn, $63 mn, 14.1%).

Mobileye announced two cloud-enhanced L2+ ADAS awards, with a top 5 global OEM from Asia and a top 10 global OEM from Japan. The Stellantis cloud-enhanced business expanded to European platforms from US vehicles only.
GS keeps its Neutral rating. The 12-month price target is cut to $7 from $8, based on 9x (from 10x, reflecting lower market multiples) applied to Q5-Q8 EBITDA estimates ex. SBC.

GS expects L2+ products (Surround ADAS and Cloud-Enhanced) to support improved ASPs, especially from 2028 onward. Eyes-off consumer vehicles, AVs and humanoid robotics could be material over the medium to longer term.

GS flags limited L3/L4 consumer program awards in recent years, execution and cost risk from the vertically integrated robotaxi approach, and an overhang from the VW business, since VW is reportedly considering changes to its product roadmap.

3Q26 adjusted gross margin fell about 300 bps y/y to about 63.8%, below GS at 65.5% and the Street at 64.6%. The causes were lower pricing, a higher mix of China OEM shipments, and higher SuperVision volumes and memory cost pass-throughs, which together cost about 100 bps versus company expectations.
3Q26 adjusted operating margin rose to about 18.1% from 14.7% y/y, helped by the R&D incentive the company began receiving in 2026. This compares with GS at 17.1% and the Street at 16.4%.

FY26 SuperVision shipment expectation raised to about 65k from about 60k, after 3Q shipments of over 15k. SuperVision volumes are expected to step down significantly q/q in 4Q. EyeQ shipments are still about 39 mn units.
Management expects 4Q ASP to benefit from memory cost pass-through revenue versus 1H26, and expects 2027 ASP to be flattish y/y.

Mobileye's own robotaxi plan: vehicle integration starts early 2027, with about 100 vehicles in 2027 (possibly all in one city). Customers began autonomous ridepooling in Hamburg with safety drivers and closed user-group testing in Orlando.

GS cut its 2027 EPS (including SBC) to -$0.05 from $0.00, with 2026 and 2028 unchanged at $0.05. The 2026 change reflects slightly higher revenue and slightly lower margins. The 2027 revenue estimate was lowered to $2,060 mn from $2,090 mn.

market_movers.rationale: GS cut the price target to $7 from $8 on a lower multiple (9x vs 10x) applied to Q5-Q8 EBITDA ex. SBC, and kept Neutral. The stock closed at $7.06, implying 0.8% downside.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported: revenue $492 mn (down 3.1% q/q, down 2.4% y/y) vs GS $476.8 mn and FactSet consensus $477 mn. Non-GAAP operating income ex. SBC $89 mn vs GS $81.3 mn and consensus $78 mn. Non-GAAP EPS ex. SBC $0.12 vs GS and consensus $0.10. Non-GAAP EPS including SBC was -$0.01, in line with GS at -$0.01.
3Q26 reported: adjusted gross margin ex. SBC 63.8% vs GS 65.5% and consensus 64.6%. Adjusted operating margin ex. SBC 18.1% vs GS 17.1% and consensus 16.4%.

3Q26 reported: EyeQ and SuperVision systems shipped 9.5 mn vs GS and consensus 9.4 mn. Average ASP $49.1 vs GS $48.3 and consensus $48.4, down 5.0% y/y. Pass-through memory cost revenue was about $7 mn at zero gross margin.

FY26 company guidance (updated after the 3Q26 print): revenue $1,995-$2,020 mn (prior $1,970-$2,020 mn), midpoint $2,007.5 mn vs GS estimate $1,991.6 mn and FactSet consensus $2,006 mn. Adjusted operating income $380-$420 mn (prior $365-$425 mn), midpoint $400 mn vs GS $394.7 mn and consensus $401 mn. Implied margin at the midpoint 19.9% vs 19.8% prior.

Implied 4Q26 guidance (derived from the FY26 guidance): revenue $437-$462 mn, midpoint $449.5 mn vs consensus $463 mn. Non-GAAP operating income $41-$81 mn, midpoint $61 mn vs consensus $73 mn (16.4% below) and GS $63.4 mn. Implied margin at the midpoint 13.6% vs consensus 15.8%.

GS estimates (GS forecasts): FY26E revenue $2,008.1 mn (old $1,991.6 mn), FY27E $2,060.3 mn (old $2,090.4 mn), FY28E $2,288.9 mn (old $2,290.9 mn). EPS including SBC FY26E/27E/28E $0.05/-$0.05/$0.05 (old $0.05/$0.00/$0.05). EPS ex. SBC $0.50/$0.40/$0.50.
Mobileye ended 3Q26 with $1.3 bn in cash and equivalents and repurchased $9 mn of shares in the quarter.
risk_factors: New design wins: securing more or fewer than GS expects would change the upside.
Rate of ADAS/AV penetration in the market.
Auto production growth versus GS expectations, which drives chip shipments.
Lower or higher ASPs and margins.
Corporate actions, including a potential stock sell-down by the controlling shareholder.
VW business outlook, with media reports that VW is considering changes to its product roadmap.
Execution and cost risk in the vertically integrated robotaxi business.
Very limited L3/L4 consumer program awards in recent years.
vol_and_positioning: Stock performance: -16.3% over 3 months, -21.9% over 6 months, -47.4% over 12 months in absolute terms. Relative to the S&P 500: -19.7%, -28.0% and -53.2%.
GS cites potential stock sell-down by Mobileye's controlling shareholder as a key risk.

tension_points.bull_case: New cloud-enhanced L2+ awards with a top 5 and a top 10 global OEM, plus Stellantis expansion to European platforms, suggest eyes-on ADAS grows meaningfully and supports higher ASPs from 2028 onward. Eyes-off consumer, AV and humanoid robotics add medium-to-longer-term optionality.
tension_points.bear_case: L3/L4 consumer awards have been very limited, the vertically integrated robotaxi entry carries execution and cost risk, and VW's potential roadmap changes are an overhang. Implied 4Q26 EBIT guidance is below the Street.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Fewer design wins than GS expects, lower ASPs or margins, weaker auto production, or a sell-down by the controlling shareholder would pressure the stock.

theme_stances.key_argument: ADAS awards point to meaningful growth in eyes-on L2+, but robotaxi execution, limited L3/L4 awards and the VW outlook offset it.
theme_stances.evidence: Progress with eyes-on ADAS awards; execution on robotaxi business and humanoids
